verdictStatement: The central repair landed. The boundedness exception is now genuinely inside SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL — 'of' carries a fourth entry naming the file 04 custody cell, whatIsSuperseded restates the scope as two displacements instead of one, and boundednessExceptionOwner names the DR-124 owners for it. That was my v4 blocker and Codex's, and the contradiction I found there is gone. But the same object was edited without its reversibility clause being carried along: 'Overturn restores the P-002-4 / P-005-2 bars' is byte-identical to v4, so the one displacement this generation added — the file 04 class rule — has no overturn at all. Codex's own repair text named reversibility as part of the fix, and 'of' also names only one of the three places that rule lives while whatIsSuperseded states it unscoped. The finding is recorded folded, with notFoldedThisSuccessor empty. That is the third generation running where a claimed-complete fold is incomplete, and it is the specific reason this cannot be an ACCEPT: the reversibility of a supersession that displaces live architecture text is not a detail.

blockers.title: The boundedness displacement was added to the supersession without reversibility, and 'of' names only one of the three places the rule lives — recorded as fully folded
blockers.subjectQuote: Overturn restores the P-002-4 / P-005-2 bars.

measurement.reversibilityWasNotCarried: I compared /proposedSupersession/standing across generations: it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to v4. The object around it was edited this generation — of gained a fourth entry, whatIsSuperseded was rewritten, boundednessExceptionOwner was added, and /proposedSupersession is on the declared roster — but the overturn sentence still names only the P-002-4 and P-005-2 bars. The displacement this generation actually added is the file 04 operational-metadata custody cell, which is neither of those. On the artifact's own terms, overturning SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL would restore the two containment prohibitions and leave the SC-OPS boundedness rule displaced.
measurement.codexAskedForExactlyThis: Codex v4 SCC-V4-B1's repair text: 'Either provide a bounded lifecycle compatible with permission v6's append-only ordering, or add the exact file-04/P-002-4/P-005-2 boundedness exception to proposedSupersession.of and whatIsSuperseded, INCLUDING RETAINED BACKUP/PURGE/LIFECYCLE CONSEQUENCES AND REVERSIBILITY.' The of/whatIsSuperseded half was done; the reversibility half was not.
measurement.ofNamesOneOfThreeInstances: of[3] scopes the displacement to '(file 04 operational-metadata custody cell)'. I measured the rule's other instances directly: route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v2.json P-005-2 contains 'Journaled/redacted/bounded' (True) and route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.json P-002-4 contains it (True). Both are owner-recorded and both would, unsuperseded, require the grant-journal bytes to be bounded. Codex named all three; 'of' names one.
measurement.ofAndWhatIsSupersededDisagree: whatIsSuperseded (2) states the displacement unscoped — 'the SC-OPS "journaled/redacted/bounded" class rule to the extent it would require dropping or bounding away grant-journal sequence records' — with no file 04 qualifier. So the two fields of the same object describe different scopes: one instance in 'of', all instances in whatIsSuperseded. Neither surviving-force list resolves it: P-005-2's retained items are doctor's own audit record, non-authority, non-rebuildability and never-a-peer-evidence-writer; P-002-4's are Plan/Run exclusion, not-rebuildable, rebuildability-stays and the completeness obligation. Boundedness appears in neither retained list.
measurement.recordedAsFolded: /honestyRepairsFromV4 asserts 'CLAUDE-V4-B1: … whatIsSuperseded names both containment and boundedness displacements; boundednessExceptionOwner names the DR-124 owners' and 'SCC-V4-B1: same boundedness displacement …; now inside SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL.of and whatIsSuperseded.' /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor is [].

blockers.whyBlocker: A supersession that displaces live architecture text and cannot be fully overturned is not a proposal, it is a one-way door. Every decision instrument in this corpus states reversibility, and this one states it for two of its three displacements while presenting itself as complete. The scope mismatch compounds it: an owner asked to concur cannot tell from the bytes whether they are being asked to displace one custody cell or the same rule wherever it appears, and the two fields that should answer that give different answers. Recording the finding as folded with an empty notFoldedThisSuccessor is what turns this from an omission into a blocker — it is the third successive generation in which a claimed-complete fold is incomplete, and that claim is the mechanism a coordinator relies on when the diff is 45 paths wide.
blockers.whatIsNotWrong: The substance is right and I am not asking for it to change. An append-only monotonic ordering journal cannot be bounded away without destroying DR-105's linearization; naming the file 04 cell explicitly was the correct and honest move, and it answers the concern I raised at v4 that nothing in this machinery reached live architecture prose. The concurrence set for the displacement is complete (M-11). What is missing is the exit.
blockers.minimumRepair: Extend /proposedSupersession/standing so overturn restores all three displacements, naming the SC-OPS boundedness rule alongside the P-002-4 / P-005-2 bars. Reconcile of[3] with whatIsSuperseded (2) — either widen of[3] to name the file-04, P-005-2 and P-002-4 instances as Codex asked, or narrow whatIsSuperseded (2) to the file 04 cell and state expressly why the two disposition instances do not bar the placement. State the retained backup/purge/lifecycle consequences for grant-journal bytes, which Codex's repair also named and which are currently only implied by the 'to the extent' clause. Then correct /honestyRepairsFromV4 and list SCC-V4-B1 in notFoldedThisSuccessor unless it is fully folded.

coordinatorNote: This is close. The architecture is settled and has been for two generations; what keeps failing is the paperwork around a single object. The pattern is worth naming because it has now recurred three times: an edit lands the substance of a finding and leaves one attached clause behind — at v4 the supersession scope, here the supersession's reversibility and the roster entry for the field being edited — and each time notFoldedThisSuccessor reports the finding as fully folded. I would suggest that whoever authors v6 treat /proposedSupersession as a unit: 'of', whatIsSuperseded, standing (including overturn), and the owner set have to be read together and edited together, because a displacement added to three of those four and missing from the fourth is exactly what B-1 is. The two SHOULD-FIX items are single-line edits. Nothing in this verdict asks for an architectural position to change, and I record explicitly that the attack I raised at v4 against the file 04 displacement — that a candidate cannot reach live architecture prose — failed on measurement: no rule in this corpus requires a route the subject has not named. I did not read the other current v5 reviewer, did not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit.
